final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence; the response reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is partly correct: the existing evidence supports aggregate operational readiness, and it does not support treating the named technician safety-note-routing context as already covered. But that clarification is not enough for compliant_with_caveats on the current record, because the caveat itself is still an unresolved compliance predicate. The governing policy requires named deployment-context evaluation gaps to be disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before clean certification. The admissible evidence shows the gap exists, shows general checks do not cover it, and shows QA treats the status as unknown. There is still no admissible evidence of an actual disclosed caveat in the certification artifact and no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance. So the Actor improved the interpretation of what the packet can and cannot support, but did not cure the compliance failure in the packet as presented.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the certification or model-card artifact actually discloses the technician safety-note-routing evaluation gap.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering launch with this named-context gap.
Technician safety-note routing is a named deployment context, and the packet still lacks its completed evaluations.
The draft model-card position remains overbroad because QA says missing evaluations are unknown rather than passed.
Aggregate readiness and general operational checks support launch readiness only in the aggregate sense and do not satisfy the named-context disclosure predicate.
